---
title: "Writing tasks for agents"
---

Agents expose incomplete intent. A useful task brief states the goal, scope, constraints, expected artefact, definition of done, and verification request.

```text
Goal: produce a small, reviewable artefact for [staff-like purpose].
Scope: inspect/change only [paths]; use fake/source-free data.
Constraints: preserve inputs; do not add credentials or network uploads.
Artefact: [file/report/check] with a short provenance note.
Done when: [objective condition].
Verify: run [focused command] and show the relevant diff/output.
```

Start with a vague request when teaching assumptions, then revise it into a bounded brief. Ask the agent to list assumptions before acting and to stop when the scope is unclear. A longer prompt is not automatically a better prompt: precision and evidence matter more than ceremony.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Try it now (5 minutes)

Rewrite “clean this analysis” into a brief with one allowed folder, one output, and one check. Compare the first plan with the revised plan. Which assumption changed the proposed tool call?
:::
